english.title: Superintendent registrar issue marriage certificate after the expiration of the applicable period
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a superintendent registrar, knowingly and wilfully issued a certificate for the marriage of **(..SPECIFY THE PARTIES TO THE MARRIAGE..) after **(..SPECIFY DATE OF EXPIRY..), being the date of expiration of the period which was, in relation to that marriage, the applicable period for the purposes of section 33 of the Marriage Act 1949
english.legislation: Contrary to section 75(3)(b) of the Marriage Act 1949.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The term 'certificates' of a superintendent registrar is substituted by a 'marriage schedule' from the 4th May 2021 by the Marriage Regulations 2021 (SI 2021/411). For offences which occur from this date, please see H22869.
(ii) Section 33(3) of the Marriage Act 1949 provides that "the applicable period, in relation to a marriage, is the period beginning with the day on which the notice of marriage was entered in the marriage notice book, or in an approved electronic form by virtue of section 27(4A), and ending (a) in the case of a marriage which is to be solemnized in pursuance of section 26(1)(dd), 37 or 38, on the expiry of three months; and (b) in the case of any other marriage, on the expiry of twelve months.
